subject: BlueSpan Health — where requests execute, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer Q&A
messages:

Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs on where data is processed + subprocessors for POC

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for walking us through the POC scope yesterday. Before we proceed to legal and procurement, BlueSpan needs a crisp answer on three things for our security review:

1) Where will our inference requests be executed (region/hops) if we use the hosted API?
2) Which subprocessors handle request execution, caching, and logs?
3) If a request falls back (regional capacity / model variant fallback), could data transit outside the US?

We're trying to map data flows for our InfoSec team and want to be explicit on cross-border transfer risk. If you can send a short plain-language summary and any simple diagram or inventory, that would be ideal.

Eliza Turner

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where data is processed + subprocessors for POC

Hi Eliza — thanks, and great questions. Short answers up front, followed by a bit more detail and attachments.

Summary (plain-language):
- Default Hosted API: customer requests are executed in the US region (primary: us-east1) by Redwood-managed compute.
- Subprocessors: we run inference on cloud compute (GCP us-east1) and use cloud object storage (GCS), and a small set of telemetry/storage partners listed in the attached inventory.
- Cross-border fallback: by default, we will not route requests outside the chosen region for compliance-tier customers. For standard Hosted customers, brief transient handoffs can occur (e.g., for model fallback or overflow) but we provide options to pin region or use Dedicated/Private to avoid that entirely.

More detail:
- Execution locations: Hosted API routes to the nearest healthy pool, typically us-east1 for your tenant. We offer region pinning on Hosted for enterprise POCs (contractual). Dedicated capacity and Private deployment guarantee locality per the contract.
- Fallback behavior: If we cannot serve a request in the pinned region (capacity outage), routing will prefer another US region where possible. We only route to non-US regions in the case of explicit customer configuration or if no US capacity is available and the customer has accepted fallbacks in their policy.
- Subprocessor inventory: included as redwood-subproc-inventory.pdf — shows compute hosts, storage, logging partners, and our KMS provider.
- Caching and logs: prefix/KV caching is ephemeral and TTL-limited; access logs and telemetry are stored for a configurable retention period. We can shorten retention and exclude request payloads for the POC.

I attached: redwood-subproc-inventory.pdf (list + short descriptions). I'm happy to produce a one-page flow diagram (we can use the BlueSpan data-map template) — copying Naomi to help pull a simple visual.

Next steps: if you want a strict no-cross-border guarantee for the POC, we can propose a Dedicated pool reserved in us-east or a Private deploy (customer-managed VPC). Either adds procurement steps but gives contractual locality guarantees.

Best,

Hi Eliza / Rajiv — jumping in with the action matrix and a recommended minimal config for the POC. See attached BlueSpan mapping.

Action matrix (one-pager):
- Model fallback that causes cross-region routing: Who = Redwood routing service; Region = only if US capacity exhausted OR customer has international fallback enabled; Deletion/TLL = ephemeral KV cache (seconds-minutes) + no persistent payload storage in fallback flow.
- Telemetry/logs: Who = telemetry subprocessor (listed in inventory); Region = US; Default storage = metrics + request metadata; Full request payloads are not retained by telemetry unless explicitly enabled. We can toggle that off for your POC.
- Deletion request (day 30): Who = Redwood ops + storage subprocessor; Process = we run a scoped erase job across object storage and telemetry indexes; Confirmation = signed erase report delivered within 72 hours for POC commits.

Recommended POC config to avoid surprises:
1) Hosted API with region pin to us-east1 (contract clause).
2) Disable payload retention and shorten telemetry retention to 7 days.
3) Include a deletion milestone (Day 30) with confirmation.

Attached: bluespan-data-map.xlsx (visual), redwood-subproc-inventory.pdf (already sent).

Happy to walk through the matrix on a short call — Mateo / Karthik can join to confirm technical steps.

Thanks,
